title: Websites for schools and tutoring businesses
meta_description: Creosote Labs builds websites, enrollment forms, and parent portals for schools and tutoring businesses, quoted at a fixed price after a scoping call.
h1: Website and web application development for schools and tutoring businesses
intro: The website for a school or tutoring business is where families compare programs, check tuition and hours, and decide whether to reach out. Many are built on Wix, Squarespace, or WordPress, with a Google Form or a link to Calendly for inquiries and a PDF for the enrollment packet. Tutoring centers often want families to book an assessment or a trial session directly, and schools often need an application process that does not depend on paper forms and email attachments.

Creosote Labs builds marketing sites with clear program descriptions, tuition, and a way to book or apply, along with the customer-facing tools behind them. That can be an online enrollment application, a trial session booking form that lands on the tutor's calendar, or a parent portal where families see schedules, invoices, and progress reports. Projects include hosting and domain setup, and we hand over the site with documentation so staff can update it.
projects: A marketing site for a tutoring center with program pages, pricing, tutor profiles, and a trial session booking form.
An online enrollment application for a private school that collects family details, documents, and a deposit in one flow.
A parent portal where families view upcoming sessions, download invoices, and read term progress reports.
A summer program registration page with session capacity limits, waitlists, and automatic confirmation emails.
A tutor-facing web application for logging sessions and notes from a phone between appointments.

faqs.q: How is a school website priced?
faqs.a: Website and application projects are quoted after a scoping call. Pricing is fixed for the agreed scope, with no hourly billing.

faqs.q: Can families pay tuition or deposits through the site?
faqs.a: Yes. Enrollment and booking tools can collect payments through a processor such as Stripe or Square, and the scoping call covers which payments belong on the site and which stay in the billing system.

faqs.q: Who updates the site after it launches?
faqs.a: The school's own staff. Every project ends with a handover and written documentation covering how to edit pages, programs, tuition, and forms, and hosting and domain configuration are set up as part of the project.
